questions.text:
The relation book (title,price) contains the titles and prices of different books. Assuming that no two books have the same price, what does the following SQL query list?
 select title
from book as B
where (select count(*)
    from book as T
    where T.price>B.price) < 5
questions.solution:
For each book B, the subquery counts books more expensive than B. If fewer than 5 are more expensive (0-4), B is among the top 5.

Answer: Titles of the five most expensive books

questions.text:
Let R(a,b,c) and S(d,e,f) be two relations in which d is the foreign key of S that refers to the primary key of R. Consider the following four operations R and S

I. Insert into R
II. Insert into S
III. Delete from R
IV. Delete from S

Which of the following can cause violation of the referential integrity constraint above?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Insert into S with a d value that does not exist in R [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] violation (II).
- Delete from R a tuple still referred to by S [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] violation (III).
- Inserting into R or deleting from S cannot create a dangling reference.

Answer: Both II and III

questions.text: Consider the join of a relation R with a relation S. If R has m tuples and S has n tuples then the maximum and minimum sizes of the join respectively are
questions.solution:
Maximum: if every tuple matches every tuple (e.g. all join values equal), the result is m [latex]\times[/latex] n. Minimum: if nothing matches, 0.

Answer: mn and 0

questions.text:
Consider the following databases chedule with two transactions, T1 and T2.
[latex]S=r_{2}(X);r_{1}(X);r_{2}(Y);w_{1}(X);r_{1}(Y);w_{2}(X);a_{1};a_{2}[/latex]
where [latex]r_{i}(Z)[/latex] denotes a read operation by transaction [latex]T_{i}[/latex] on avariable Z, [latex]w_{i}(Z)[/latex] denotes a write operation by [latex]T_{i}[/latex] on avariable Z and [latex]a_{i}[/latex] denotes an abort by transaction [latex]T_{i}[/latex].
Which one of the following statements about the above schedule is TRUE?
questions.solution:
No transaction reads a value written by the other before it ends: T1 reads X before T2 writes it, and T2's reads happen before T1's write. So when T1 aborts, T2 does not need to be aborted: no cascading abort.

It is not strict, because [latex]w_2(X)[/latex] overwrites [latex]w_1(X)[/latex] while T1 is still active.

Answer: S does not have a cascading abort

options: S is recoverable,but has a cascading abort
S does not have a cascading abort
